identification.summary: Curious Gorge is Google Threat Analysis Group's (TAG) name for a China-linked cyber espionage group that TAG attributes to the PLA Strategic Support Force (SSF) [S2]. TAG reported campaigns against government and military organizations in Ukraine, Russia, Kazakhstan and Mongolia [S3][S2].
identification.firstObserved: March 2022: TAG described campaigns observed in the preceding two weeks [S3]. Earlier activity is not established in the sources gathered.
identification.notes: Google TAG name. The encyclopedia record lists UNC3742 (Mandiant / Google TI) as an alias, via an imported community (MISP Galaxy) mapping; no cited source read in this pass states it directly. Microsoft has no mapped name in this record. No malware families are associated with the actor in Malpedia [S5].

attribution.sponsor: People's Republic of China, specifically the PLA Strategic Support Force, per Google TAG as reported by Security Affairs [S2].
attribution.confidence: Confidence level not stated in the secondary coverage gathered [S2]. This is a vendor (Google TAG) attribution only; no government attribution was found.
attribution.basis: Google TAG assessment; the evidentiary basis is not described in the secondary coverage read [S2][S3].

objectives: Espionage against government, military, logistics and manufacturing organizations in Ukraine, Russia and Central Asia, inferred from the victim set TAG reported [S2]. Specific collection requirements are not stated in the sources.

targeting.notes: March 2022: government and military organizations in Ukraine, Russia, Kazakhstan and Mongolia [S3][S2]. Later TAG update: long-running campaigns against multiple Russian government organizations including the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, plus compromises of multiple Russian defense contractors and manufacturers and a Russian logistics company [S2]. TAG said the activity does not greatly affect Google products but it notified victims [S3].

capabilities.summary: Initial access vectors, tooling and exploits are not described in the sources I could read; TAG's March 2022 post reportedly listed IP addresses used in campaigns [S1]. Malpedia lists no associated malware families [S5].

campaigns.name: Campaigns against Ukraine, Russia, Kazakhstan, Mongolia
campaigns.summary: TAG reported malicious campaigns against military and government organizations in Russia, Ukraine, Mongolia and Kazakhstan over the prior two weeks, in an update that also covered COLDRIVER and Ghostwriter [S3][S1].

campaigns.name: Continued activity against Russian government and industry
campaigns.summary: TAG update: long-running campaigns against multiple Russian government organizations, including the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, continued; over the prior week TAG identified compromises of multiple Russian defense contractors and manufacturers and a Russian logistics company [S2].

campaigns.name: Google 'Fog of War' report
campaigns.summary: Google published a report on how the Ukraine conflict changed the cyber threat landscape; the report's own treatment of Curious Gorge was not read [S4].

diamond.adversary: China-linked group attributed by Google TAG to the PLA SSF [S2].
diamond.infrastructure: TAG published IP addresses for the March 2022 campaigns [S1]; details not retrieved.
diamond.victim: Government, military, defense industrial, logistics and manufacturing organizations in Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan and Mongolia [S2][S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: PRC collection on Russia, Ukraine and Central Asian neighbors during the Russia-Ukraine war, including against a nominal partner (Russia) [S2]. Motivations beyond that are not stated in sources.

gaps: Google TAG primary posts and the Fog of War PDF could not be fetched (blog.google unreachable from this environment); all facts rely on secondary coverage and search summaries. Primary posts were not opened.
The exact TAG post dates (March and May 2022) are given at month precision only.
TTPs, malware, exploits, phishing lures and infrastructure are not documented in the sources read.
UNC3742 equivalence is from an imported community mapping and not verified against a Google/Mandiant statement.
Attribution confidence and evidence behind the PLA SSF assessment are unknown; note the SSF was reorganized in 2024 so unit naming may be outdated.
No activity after 2023 was found; current status is unknown.
Overlap with other tracked PRC clusters targeting Russia (other vendors) was not assessed.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Government, defense-industrial, logistics and manufacturing networks in Russia, Ukraine and Central Asia are the observed terrain [S2][S3]. STEP 2: The actor operates against a nominal partner state, showing PRC collection is not limited to adversaries [S2]. STEP 3: Tradecraft is not documented in the sources; templating is not possible. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued espionage against regional government, military and logistics targets [S2]. MDCOA (speculative) is extension of the same access to logistics and manufacturing networks supporting regional military supply chains. Candidate indicators: the IP addresses in TAG's March 2022 post [S1] (not retrieved here).
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track vendor reporting on PRC activity in Eurasia as indicator of PRC regional collection priorities. (2) Authorities and mission assurance: no US-targeted activity is evidenced in the sources, so treat as a regional intelligence-gap item rather than a defended-network threat. (3) Coordination: retrieve the primary TAG posts and IOC lists through intelligence channels before use.

provenance.importedSummary: Curious Gorge, a group TAG attributes to China's PLA SSF, has conducted campaigns against government and military organizations in Ukraine, Russia, Kazakhstan, and Mongolia. The actor has remained active against government, military, logistics and manufacturing organizations in Ukraine, Russia and Central Asia. In Russia, long running campaigns against multiple government organizations have continued, including the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Over the past week, TAG identified additional compromises impacting multiple Russian defense contractors and manufacturers and a Russian logistics company.
